newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek financial mkts idle in pre-Christmas trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek financial mkts idle in pre-Christmas trade.

text.p: Greek financial markets were idling in late pre-Christmas trading and the Bank of Greece drained overnight funds at an unchanged 12.40 percent in a calm market, dealers said.

"The Bank of Greece soaked up overnight funds at an unchanged 12.40 percent and that's about it," a foreign bank dealer said. "Money, bonds and everything else just sit tight with players unwilling to open positions."
The market focus now shifts to Friday's auction, the dealer said.
The finance ministry announced that its three-year, 100 billion drachma bond to be auctioned on December 27 will feature a lower coupon at 10.70 percent from 11 percent previously.
The seven-year, 200 billion drachma FRN to be auctioned the same day will also feature a lower base rate of 11.20 percent, down from 11.50 percent at the previous auction.
The mark was quoted at 159.15/25 drachmas from Tuesday's 159.200 fix, the dollar at 247.51/61 drachmas from 247.500 and the Ecu at 306.33/40 from 306.350 drachmas.
